# The common English words the masker keeps (internal/threadctx/mask.go): the
# 10000 most frequent words of the Wiktionary frequency lists of English as used
# in television and movie scripts, each kept when Webster's Second
# International Dictionary lists it, or the word an -s, -es, -ed, -d or -ing
# ending inflects, in lower case, or when it is a contraction: a word ending in
# n't, 'll, 're, 've, 'd or 'm; a word ending in 's whose first part also takes
# 'll, 're, 've, 'd or 'm among the frequent words ("it's" beside "it'll"), or
# is let, here, now, when, all, whatever, whoever or an indefinite pronoun
# ("let's", "here's", "something's"); or
# a part of at most two letters before an apostrophe and a word of the
# dictionary or another part of at most two letters ("y'all", "ma'am"). Any
# other word written with an apostrophe is left out: a name's ("teal'c") or a
# possessive's ("emily's"), whose suffix the masker keeps apart from the word
# before it.
